definitions.definition: the act of discussing something with somebody or with a group of people before making a decision about it
examples: a consultation document/paper/period/process
The decision was taken after close consultation with local residents.
acting in consultation with all the departments involved
definitions.definition_vi: hành động thảo luận điều gì đó với ai đó hoặc với một nhóm người trước khi đưa ra quyết định về việc đó

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a formal meeting to discuss something
examples: There have been extensive consultations between the two countries.
definitions.definition_vi: một cuộc họp chính thức để thảo luận về một cái gì đó

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a meeting with an expert, especially a doctor, to get advice or treatment
examples: A 30-minute consultation will cost £50.
definitions.definition_vi: cuộc gặp với một chuyên gia, đặc biệt là bác sĩ, để được tư vấn hoặc điều trị

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: the act of looking for information in a book, etc.
examples: There is a large collection of texts available for consultation on-screen.
definitions.definition_vi: hành động tìm kiếm thông tin trong một cuốn sách, v.v.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a person who buys goods or uses services
examples: COMPARE producer
consumer spending/demand
links between producers and consumers
Health-conscious consumers want more information about the food they buy.
a consumer society (= one where buying and selling is considered to be very important)
a consumer watchdog (= somebody whose job is to protect consumers' rights)
The consumer (= consumers as a group) is well served by competition.
This tool may be considered too expensive for the average consumer.
consumers of news/electricity/healthcare
providers and consumers of public services
We need to educate consumers about this technology.
definitions.definition_vi: người mua hàng hóa hoặc sử dụng dịch vụ

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the feeling that somebody/something is without value and deserves no respect at all
examples: She looked at him with contempt.
I shall treat that suggestion with the contempt it deserves.
His treatment of his children is beneath contempt (= so bad that it is not even worth feeling contempt for).
Politicians seem to be generally held in contempt by ordinary people.
They had shown a contempt for the values she thought important.
definitions.definition_vi: cảm giác rằng ai đó/cái gì đó không có giá trị và không đáng được tôn trọng chút nào

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a lack of worry or fear about rules, danger, etc.
examples: The firefighters showed a contempt for their own safety.
His remarks betray a staggering contempt for the truth (= are completely false).
definitions.definition_vi: thiếu lo lắng hoặc sợ hãi về các quy tắc, nguy hiểm, v.v.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the crime of refusing to obey an order made by a court; not showing respect for a court or judge
examples: He could be jailed for two years for contempt.
She was held in contempt for refusing to testify.
definitions.definition_vi: tội không chấp hành mệnh lệnh của tòa án; không thể hiện sự tôn trọng đối với tòa án hoặc thẩm phán

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: knowing somebody/something very well may cause you to lose respect for them/itWord Origin
examples: late Middle English: from Latin contemptus, from contemnere, from con- (expressing intensive force) + temnere ‘despise’.
definitions.definition_vi: biết quá rõ về ai đó/điều gì đó có thể khiến bạn mất đi sự tôn trọng đối với họ/itWord Origin

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: anger between people who disagree
examples: SYNONYM dispute
One area of contention is the availability of nursery care.
Privatization of the health service remains a point of contention.
There is no contention between the two groups.
definitions.definition_vi: sự tức giận giữa những người không đồng ý

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a belief or an opinion that you express, especially in an argument
examples: It is our client's contention that the fire was an accident.
I would reject that contention.
definitions.definition_vi: một niềm tin hoặc một ý kiến ​​mà bạn thể hiện, đặc biệt là trong một cuộc tranh luận

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a subject that causes people to disagree
examples: Where to go on holiday is always a bone of contention in our family.
definitions.definition_vi: một chủ đề khiến mọi người không đồng ý

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: with a chance of winning something
examples: Only three teams are now in contention for the title.
definitions.definition_vi: với cơ hội giành được thứ gì đó

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: without a chance of winning something
examples: The Jaguars are now out of contention.
The Comets were eliminated from play-off contention.
definitions.definition_vi: không có cơ hội giành được thứ gì đó

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the situation in which something happens and that helps you to understand it
examples: Such databases are being used in a wide range of contexts.
to examine the wider/broader context of the war
the historical/cultural/social context
The government must consider the context of the protests.
This kind of propaganda is used in many different contexts.
Institutions provide a context in which individuals can take on different roles.
This speech needs to be set in the context of Britain in the 1960s.
His decision can only be understood in context.
I think it's important to put this into context.
A ceasefire is the essential context for meaningful negotiations.
definitions.definition_vi: tình huống trong đó điều gì đó xảy ra và điều đó giúp bạn hiểu nó

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the words that come just before and after a word, phrase or statement and help you to understand its meaning
examples: You should be able to guess the meaning of the word from the context.
The context of the quotation makes her meaning quite clear.
This quotation has been taken out of context (= repeated without referring to the rest of the text).
You need to look at the words in context.
definitions.definition_vi: những từ đứng trước và sau một từ, cụm từ hoặc câu phát biểu và giúp bạn hiểu ý nghĩa của nó

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: an official written agreement
examples: SEE ALSO social contract
All employees have a written contract of employment.
a research/modelling/recording contract
a lucrative government contract
to enter into/negotiate/sign a contract with the supplier
These clauses form part of the contract between buyer and seller.
a contract for the supply of vehicles
to win/be awarded a contract to build a new school
to renew/extend/terminate/cancel a contract
I was on a three-year contract that expired last week.
She is under contract to (= has a contract to work for) a major American computer firm.
The phone costs several hundred dollars more out of contract (= without a contract with a phone company).
The midfielder will be out of contract at the end of the season (= his contract with his club will have finished).
a contract worker (= one employed on a contract for a fixed period of time)
Under the terms of the contract the job should have been finished yesterday.
They were sued for breach of contract (= not doing what they agreed to do in a contract).
He had a release clause written into his contract.
The offer has been accepted, subject to contract (= the agreement is not official until the contract is signed).
definitions.definition_vi: một thỏa thuận bằng văn bản chính thức

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: an agreement to kill somebody for money
examples: She took out a contract on her ex-husband.
He has a contract out on you.
definitions.definition_vi: một thỏa thuận giết ai đó vì tiền

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to give something, especially money or goods, to help achieve or provide something
examples: Do you wish to contribute?
Would you like to contribute to our collection?
to contribute to your pension
Check with your financial planner to make sure that you are contributing the correct amounts.
We contributed £5 000 to the earthquake fund.
definitions.definition_vi: đưa cái gì đó, đặc biệt là tiền hoặc hàng hóa, để giúp đạt được hoặc cung cấp cái gì đó

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to be one of the causes of something
examples: Human error may have been a contributing factor.
It is well known that UV radiation contributes to the development of skin cancer.
Investment in transport contributes to overall economic growth.
Medical negligence was said to have contributed to her death.
England fans are contributing hugely to the success of this event.
US policy has contributed to the problem.
Several factors may be contributing to the fall in the number of applicants.
definitions.definition_vi: là một trong những nguyên nhân của cái gì đó

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to increase, improve or add to something
examples: Immigrants have contributed to British culture in many ways.
Parental involvement contributes significantly to children's learning.
Hall's work contributed greatly to our knowledge of the disease.
This book contributes little to our understanding of the subject.
definitions.definition_vi: để tăng, cải thiện hoặc thêm vào một cái gì đó

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to write things for a newspaper, book, website, etc. or a radio or television programme; to speak during a meeting or conversation, especially to give your opinion
examples: The blog now has about 20 people contributing regularly.
a contributing editor
We hope everyone will contribute to the discussion.
Associated Press contributed to this report.
He contributed a piece on Canadian law.
She contributed a number of articles to the magazine.
definitions.definition_vi: viết bài cho một tờ báo, cuốn sách, trang web, v.v. hoặc một chương trình phát thanh hoặc truyền hình; để nói chuyện trong một cuộc họp hoặc cuộc trò chuyện, đặc biệt là để đưa ra ý kiến ​​của bạn

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to decide and state officially in court that somebody is guilty of a crime
examples: OPPOSITE acquit
He was convicted of fraud.
a convicted murderer
There wasn’t enough evidence to convict her.
definitions.definition_vi: quyết định và tuyên bố chính thức trước tòa rằng ai đó phạm tội

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: fairly cold; not hot or warm
examples: cool air/water
a cool breeze/drink/climate
Cooler weather is forecast for the weekend.
These plants prefer cooler temperatures.
Let's sit in the shade and keep cool.
The wooden shutters help keep the building cool.
Store lemons in a cool dry place.
definitions.definition_vi: khá lạnh; không nóng hoặc ấm

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: helping you keep cool
examples: Wear light, cool clothing but try to avoid shorts.
definitions.definition_vi: giúp bạn luôn mát mẻ

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: making you feel pleasantly cool
examples: a room painted in cool greens and blues
definitions.definition_vi: khiến bạn cảm thấy mát mẻ dễ chịu

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: used to show that you admire or approve of somebody/something because they are/it is fashionable, attractive and often different
examples: Doesn't she look cool in those sunglasses?
He's a really cool guy.
You look pretty cool with that new haircut.
It's a cool movie.
She has lots of cool ideas.
definitions.definition_vi: dùng để thể hiện rằng bạn ngưỡng mộ hoặc tán thành ai/cái gì vì họ/nó hợp thời trang, hấp dẫn và thường khác biệt

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: used to describe something that you like or enjoy
examples: We had such a cool time with Ed and his friends.
I really hope you can come—it'd be so cool!
It was totally cool to see him in real life.
It's really cool you came back!
definitions.definition_vi: được sử dụng để mô tả một cái gì đó mà bạn thích hoặc tận hưởng

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: used to show that you approve of something or agree to a suggestion
examples: We're meeting Jake for lunch and we can go on the yacht in the afternoon.’ ‘Cool!’
Can you come at 10.30 tomorrow?’ ‘That's cool.’
‘Yeah, sure. That sounds cool,’ he replied.
I was surprised that she got the job, but I'm cool with it (= it's not a problem for me).
She's completely cool about what happened.
definitions.definition_vi: được sử dụng để cho thấy rằng bạn chấp nhận một cái gì đó hoặc đồng ý với một đề nghị

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: calm; not excited, angry or emotional
examples: Keep cool!
Just stay cool and don't panic.
She tried to remain cool, calm and collected (= calm).
He has a cool head (= he stays calm in an emergency).
definitions.definition_vi: điềm tĩnh; không vui mừng, tức giận hoặc xúc động

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: not friendly, interested or enthusiastic
examples: They gave the prime minister a cool reception.
Her voice was cool and dismissive.
She was decidedly cool about the proposal.
He has been cool towards me ever since we had that argument.
definitions.definition_vi: không thân thiện, quan tâm hoặc nhiệt tình

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: calm and confident in a way that lacks respect for other people, but makes people admire you even if they don't approve
examples: She just took his keys and walked out with them, cool as you please.
He was a cool customer. No one would think to look for him in a city where he’d been arrested for killing a cop.
definitions.definition_vi: điềm tĩnh và tự tin theo cách thiếu tôn trọng người khác nhưng lại khiến mọi người ngưỡng mộ bạn ngay cả khi họ không tán thành

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: used about a sum of money to emphasize how large it is
examples: The car cost a cool thirty thousand.
definitions.definition_vi: được sử dụng về một số tiền để nhấn mạnh mức độ lớn của nó

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: very calm and showing control, especially in a difficult situation
examples: George is cool as a cucumber and this should be just another operation for him.
definitions.definition_vi: rất bình tĩnh và thể hiện sự kiểm soát, đặc biệt trong tình huống khó khăn

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: to deal with a situation in a calm way and not show what you are really feeling
examples: I decided to play it cool and act like I had actually forgotten all about it.
definitions.definition_vi: để giải quyết một tình huống một cách bình tĩnh và không thể hiện những gì bạn đang thực sự cảm thấy

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: to consider a problem or possibility very carefully and without hurrying
examples: We need to take a long, hard look at all the options.
definitions.definition_vi: xem xét một vấn đề hoặc khả năng một cách rất cẩn thận và không vội vàng

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: very fashionable
examples: The assistants look like they're too cool for school.
definitions.definition_vi: rất thời trang

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to work together with somebody else in order to achieve something
examples: The two groups agreed to cooperate with each other.
They had cooperated closely in the planning of the project.
definitions.definition_vi: làm việc cùng với ai khác để đạt được điều gì đó

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to be helpful by doing what somebody asks you to do
examples: Their captors told them they would be killed unless they cooperated.
The company has agreed to cooperate with the employment survey.
definitions.definition_vi: trở nên hữu ích bằng cách làm những gì ai đó yêu cầu bạn làm

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: involving doing something together or working together with others towards a shared aim
examples: Cooperative activity is essential to effective community work.
The documentary was a cooperative effort by film-makers from five countries.
This is a cooperative venture with the University of Copenhagen.
definitions.definition_vi: liên quan đến việc làm điều gì đó cùng nhau hoặc làm việc cùng với những người khác hướng tới một mục tiêu chung

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: helpful by doing what you are asked to do
examples: OPPOSITE uncooperative
Employees will generally be more cooperative if their views are taken seriously.
definitions.definition_vi: hữu ích bằng cách làm những gì bạn được yêu cầu làm

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: owned and run by the people involved, with the profits shared by them
examples: a cooperative farm
The cooperative movement started in Britain in the nineteenth century.
definitions.definition_vi: được sở hữu và điều hành bởi những người liên quan, với lợi nhuận được chia sẻ bởi họ

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the most important or central part of something
examples: SEE ALSO Common Core
This report goes to the core of the argument.
Dutch paintings form the core of the collection.
Concern for the environment is at the core of our policies.
Our need for love lies at the very core of our being.
She claimed the original six countries of the EU constituted an inner core within the larger union.
None of the characters really gives the film an emotional core.
definitions.definition_vi: phần quan trọng nhất hoặc trung tâm của một cái gì đó

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the central part of an object
examples: the earth’s core
the core of a nuclear reactor
The standards of housing and education are often lower in the older urban cores (= the centres of towns or cities).
definitions.definition_vi: phần trung tâm của một vật thể

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the hard central part of a fruit such as an apple, that contains the seeds
examples: an apple core
definitions.definition_vi: phần cứng ở giữa của quả như quả táo, chứa hạt

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: the muscles of the lower back and stomach area which help you to maintain good balance, etc.
examples: Your posture will improve as your core becomes stronger.
definitions.definition_vi: các cơ ở vùng lưng dưới và vùng bụng giúp bạn giữ thăng bằng tốt, v.v.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a small group of people who take part in a particular activity
examples: He gathered a small core of advisers around him.
definitions.definition_vi: một nhóm nhỏ những người tham gia vào một hoạt động cụ thể

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: so that the whole of a thing or a person is affected
examples: She was shaken to the core by the news.
He's a politician to the core (= in all his attitudes and actions).
definitions.definition_vi: để toàn bộ sự việc hoặc con người bị ảnh hưởng

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a large business company
examples: multinational corporations
the Chrysler corporation
definitions.definition_vi: một công ty kinh doanh lớn

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: an organization or a group of organizations that is recognized by law as a single unit
examples: urban development corporations
definitions.definition_vi: một tổ chức hoặc một nhóm các tổ chức được pháp luật công nhận là một đơn vị duy nhất

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a group of people elected to govern a large town or city and provide public services
examples: the Lord Mayor and Corporation of the City of London
definitions.definition_vi: một nhóm người được bầu để quản lý một thị trấn hoặc thành phố lớn và cung cấp các dịch vụ công cộng

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a person who reports news from a particular country or on a particular subject for a newspaper or a television or radio station
examples: She's the BBC's political correspondent.
a foreign/war/sports correspondent
our Delhi correspondent
definitions.definition_vi: người đưa tin tức từ một quốc gia cụ thể hoặc về một chủ đề cụ thể cho một tờ báo hoặc đài truyền hình hoặc đài phát thanh

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a person who writes letters, emails, etc. to another person
examples: She's a poor correspondent (= she does not write regularly).
He was a vivid and witty correspondent.
definitions.definition_vi: người viết thư, email, v.v. cho người khác

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: dishonest or illegal behaviour, especially of people in authority
examples: allegations of bribery and corruption
The new district attorney has promised to fight police corruption.
definitions.definition_vi: hành vi không trung thực hoặc bất hợp pháp, đặc biệt là của những người có thẩm quyền

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the act or effect of making somebody change from moral to immoral standards of behaviour
examples: He claimed that sex and violence on TV led to the corruption of young people.
definitions.definition_vi: hành động hoặc tác dụng làm cho ai đó thay đổi từ tiêu chuẩn đạo đức sang tiêu chuẩn hành vi vô đạo đức

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the form of a word or phrase that has become changed from its original form in some way; the process by which a word or phrase changes form in this way
examples: The word ‘holiday’ is a corruption of ‘holy day’.
He thought it was possible to secure the language from corruption and decay.
definitions.definition_vi: dạng của một từ hoặc cụm từ đã bị thay đổi so với dạng ban đầu của nó theo một cách nào đó; quá trình mà một từ hoặc cụm từ thay đổi hình thức theo cách này

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: the effect when data is changed by accident in a computer system due to hardware or software failure
examples: A failure of a hard disk can cause unrecoverable data corruption.
definitions.definition_vi: hiệu ứng khi dữ liệu bị thay đổi ngẫu nhiên trong hệ thống máy tính do lỗi phần cứng hoặc phần mềm

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: something that you decide when you have thought about all the information connected with the situation
examples: We can safely draw some conclusions from our discussion.
He arrived at a different conclusion.
There is abundant evidence to support this conclusion.
Other studies have yielded the same conclusion.
The final section summarizes the conclusions of the study.
I've come to the conclusion that he's not the right person for the job.
New evidence might lead to the conclusion that we are wrong.
It is too soon to reach any conclusions about voting trends.
definitions.definition_vi: điều gì đó mà bạn quyết định khi bạn đã nghĩ về tất cả thông tin liên quan đến tình huống đó

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the end of something such as a speech or a piece of writing
examples: LANGUAGE BANK AT emphasis
The conclusion of the book was disappointing.
After his death, his assistant completed chapters nine and ten and wrote the conclusion.
If we took this argument to its logical conclusion…
The film is a fitting conclusion to the series.
In conclusion (= finally), I would like to thank…
definitions.definition_vi: sự kết thúc của một cái gì đó như một bài phát biểu hoặc một đoạn văn bản

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the formal and final arrangement of something official
examples: SYNONYM completion
the successful conclusion of a trade treaty
definitions.definition_vi: sự sắp xếp chính thức và cuối cùng của một cái gì đó chính thức

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: if you say that something is a foregone conclusion, you mean that it is a result that is certain to happen
examples: The outcome of the vote is a foregone conclusion.
The result of the game was a foregone conclusion.
definitions.definition_vi: nếu bạn nói điều gì đó là một kết luận đã được định trước, bạn có ý nói rằng đó là một kết quả chắc chắn sẽ xảy ra

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to make a decision about somebody/something too quickly, before you know or have thought about all the facts
examples: There I go again—jumping to conclusions.
definitions.definition_vi: đưa ra quyết định về ai/cái gì quá nhanh, trước khi bạn biết hoặc chưa nghĩ đến tất cả sự thật

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to organize and/or do a particular activity
examples: to conduct an experiment/inquiry/investigation/interview
to conduct a survey/poll/study/review
to conduct a test/trial
to conduct research/business
There are concerns about the way in which the firm conducts its acitvities.
The battalion had been preparing to conduct operations in the same area.
Police conducted a thorough search of the building.
The negotiations have been conducted in a positive manner.
They conducted a vigorous campaign for a shorter working week.
definitions.definition_vi: để tổ chức và/hoặc thực hiện một hoạt động cụ thể

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to direct a group of people who are singing or playing music
examples: a concert by the London Philharmonic Orchestra, conducted by Marin Alsop
He conducted a programme of Sibelius and Tchaikovsky.
She will conduct works by Brahms and Schumann in tonight's concert.
She sang Gluck's Orfeo at Covent Garden, with Sir Thomas Beecham conducting.
definitions.definition_vi: chỉ đạo một nhóm người đang hát hoặc chơi nhạc

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to lead or guide somebody through or around a place
examples: a conducted tour of Athens (= one with a guide, giving information about it)
The guide conducted us around the ruins of the ancient city.
definitions.definition_vi: dẫn dắt hoặc hướng dẫn ai đó đi qua hoặc đi vòng quanh một địa điểm

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to behave in a particular way
examples: He conducted himself far better than expected.
The report challenges them to examine how they conduct themselves in the workplace.
definitions.definition_vi: cư xử theo một cách cụ thể

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to allow heat or electricity to pass along or through it
examples: Copper conducts electricity well.
definitions.definition_vi: để cho phép nhiệt hoặc điện đi qua hoặc đi qua nó

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to admit, especially formally or to the police, that you have done something wrong or illegal
examples: After hours of questioning, the suspect confessed.
She confessed to the murder.
He confessed that he had stolen the money.
She confessed to me that she had known his true identity for some time.
We persuaded her to confess her crime.
definitions.definition_vi: thừa nhận, đặc biệt là chính thức hoặc với cảnh sát, rằng bạn đã làm điều gì đó sai trái hoặc bất hợp pháp

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to admit something that you feel ashamed or embarrassed about
examples: SEE ALSO self-confessed
She was reluctant to confess her ignorance.
I must confess to knowing nothing about golf.
I confess (that) I know nothing about golf.
‘I know nothing about it,’ he confessed.
I confess myself bewildered by their explanation.
definitions.definition_vi: thừa nhận điều gì đó mà bạn cảm thấy xấu hổ hoặc xấu hổ về

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to tell God or a priest about the bad things you have done so that you can say that you are sorry and be forgiven
examples: They had confessed their sins and done their penance.
definitions.definition_vi: nói với Chúa hoặc một linh mục về những điều xấu bạn đã làm để bạn có thể nói rằng bạn xin lỗi và được tha thứ

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to hear somebody confess their sins (= the bad things they have done)Word Origin
examples: late Middle English: from Old French confesser, from Latin confessus, past participle of confiteri ‘acknowledge’, from con- (expressing intensive force) + fateri ‘declare, avow’.
definitions.definition_vi: nghe ai đó thú nhận tội lỗi của họ (= những điều xấu họ đã làm) Nguồn gốc từ

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a statement that a person makes, admitting that they are guilty of a crime; the act of making such a statement
examples: After hours of questioning by police, she made a full confession.
His confession was extracted under torture.
definitions.definition_vi: lời tuyên bố của một người thừa nhận rằng họ đã phạm tội; hành động đưa ra tuyên bố như vậy

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a statement admitting something that you are ashamed or embarrassed about; the act of making such a statement
examples: SYNONYM admission
I've a confession to make—I lied about my age.
definitions.definition_vi: một tuyên bố thừa nhận điều gì đó mà bạn xấu hổ hoặc bối rối; hành động đưa ra tuyên bố như vậy

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a private statement to a priest about the bad things that you have done; an occasion when you make such a statement
examples: The priest heard her confession and granted absolution.
I used to go to confession every Saturday as a child.
definitions.definition_vi: lời trình bày riêng với linh mục về những điều xấu bạn đã làm; một dịp khi bạn đưa ra một tuyên bố như vậy

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a statement of your religious beliefs, principles, etc.
examples: a confession of faith
definitions.definition_vi: một tuyên bố về niềm tin, nguyên tắc tôn giáo của bạn, v.v.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the feeling that you can trust, believe in and be sure about the abilities or good qualities of somebody/something
examples: SEE ALSO consumer confidence
The president's actions hardly inspire confidence.
The players all have confidence in their manager.
He believes his reforms will restore confidence in the financial markets.
The survey revealed a lack of confidence in the government.
She has the utmost confidence in her students' abilities.
Our aim is to increase public confidence in the democratic process.
The university is facing a crisis of confidence about its future role.
The new contracts have undermined the confidence of employees.
definitions.definition_vi: cảm giác mà bạn có thể tin tưởng, tin tưởng và chắc chắn về khả năng hoặc phẩm chất tốt của ai đó/điều gì đó

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a belief in your own ability to do things and be successful
examples: SEE ALSO self-confidence
People often lose confidence when they are criticized.
He gained confidence when he went to college.
Receiving compliments from my work colleagues has boosted my confidence.
The course will help you build your confidence and develop your study skills.
While girls lack confidence, boys often overestimate their abilities.
He suffers from a lack of confidence.
She answered the questions with confidence.
I didn't have any confidence in myself at school.
Winning the award has given me much more confidence in my writing.
The training programmes have given workers the confidence to take on more responsibility.
definitions.definition_vi: niềm tin vào khả năng của chính bạn để làm mọi việc và thành công

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the feeling that you are certain about something
examples: He said he wished that he shared her confidence.
They could not say with confidence that he would be able to walk again after the accident.
No one can predict with complete confidence what will happen in the financial markets.
She expressed her confidence that they would win.
definitions.definition_vi: cảm giác rằng bạn chắc chắn về điều gì đó

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a feeling of trust that somebody will keep information private
examples: It took a long time to gain her confidence (= make her feel she could trust me).
Eva told me about their relationship in confidence.
This is in the strictest confidence.
definitions.definition_vi: cảm giác tin tưởng rằng ai đó sẽ giữ thông tin riêng tư

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a secret that you tell somebody
examples: The girls exchanged confidences.
I could never forgive Mike for betraying a confidence.
definitions.definition_vi: một bí mật mà bạn nói với ai đó

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to be trusted with somebody’s secrets
examples: He is said to be very much in the president's confidence.
definitions.definition_vi: được tin cậy khi tiết lộ bí mật của ai đó

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to tell somebody secrets and personal information about yourself
examples: She took me into her confidence and told me about the problems she was facing.
She thought she might take Leo into her confidence.
definitions.definition_vi: kể cho ai đó những bí mật và thông tin cá nhân về bản thân bạn

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: feeling sure about your own ability to do things and be successful
examples: SEE ALSO self-confident
She was in a relaxed, confident mood.
Beneath his confident and charming exterior, lurked a mass of insecurities.
I was actually fairly confident about my chances.
The teacher wants the children to feel confident about asking questions when they don't understand.
He'd learned to be confident in his ability to handle anything life threw at him.
definitions.definition_vi: cảm thấy chắc chắn về khả năng của chính bạn để làm mọi việc và thành công

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: feeling certain that something will happen in the way that you want or expect
examples: The Democrats were confident of victory.
The team feels confident of winning.
We are confident about the future.
I'm confident that you will get the job.
He said he remained confident that the dispute could be resolved.
We're pretty confident we can win the case.
She was quietly confident that everything would go as planned.
definitions.definition_vi: cảm thấy chắc chắn rằng điều gì đó sẽ xảy ra theo cách mà bạn muốn hoặc mong đợi

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a situation in which people, groups or countries disagree strongly or are involved in a serious argument
examples: The violence was the result of political and ethnic conflicts.
a conflict between two cultures
His task will be to resolve potential conflicts between the British and Scottish goverments.
The prime minister wants to avoid conflict with the unions.
The government has done nothing to resolve the conflict over nurses' pay.
She found herself in conflict with her parents over her future career.
John often comes into conflict with his boss.
The terms of the will became a source of conflict within the family.
She has received training in conflict resolution.
definitions.definition_vi: một tình huống trong đó mọi người, nhóm hoặc quốc gia không đồng ý mạnh mẽ hoặc tham gia vào một cuộc tranh luận nghiêm túc

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a violent situation or period of fighting between two countries
examples: armed/military conflict
The country has experienced internal conflict over the last decade.
Hopes of ending the conflict in the region are fading.
international efforts to find a peaceful solution to the conflict
This isolated state faces the risk of another violent conflict with its neighbour.
They are engaged in a bloody conflict over the disputed territory.
A conflict between the two countries could easily spread across the whole region.
definitions.definition_vi: một tình huống bạo lực hoặc thời gian chiến đấu giữa hai nước

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a situation in which there are ideas, opinions, feelings or wishes that are opposed to each other; a situation in which it is difficult to choose
examples: Her diary was a record of her inner conflict.
The story tells of a classic conflict between love and duty.
Many of these ideas appear to be in conflict with each other.
He faced a conflict of loyalties.
a serious conflict of opinion
definitions.definition_vi: tình huống trong đó có những ý tưởng, quan điểm, cảm xúc hoặc mong muốn trái ngược nhau; một tình huống trong đó rất khó để lựa chọn

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a situation in which somebody has two jobs, aims, roles, etc. and cannot treat both of them equally and fairly at the same time
examples: There was a conflict of interest between his business dealings and his political activities.
One member of the planning committee had a conflict of interest as he lived near the proposed road.
There is often a conflict of interests between farmers and conservationists.
definitions.definition_vi: một tình huống trong đó ai đó có hai công việc, mục tiêu, vai trò, v.v. và không thể đối xử bình đẳng và công bằng với cả hai cùng một lúc

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to appear and need to be dealt with by somebody
examples: What is to be done about the economic problems confronting the country?
I was suddenly confronted by the task of rewriting the entire book.
The government found itself confronted by massive opposition.
definitions.definition_vi: xuất hiện và cần được ai đó giải quyết

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to deal with a problem or difficult situation
examples: SYNONYM face up to
She knew that she had to confront her fears.
definitions.definition_vi: để giải quyết một vấn đề hoặc tình huống khó khăn

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to face somebody so that they cannot avoid seeing and hearing you, especially in an unfriendly or dangerous situation
examples: This was the first time he had confronted an armed robber.
Confronted by an angry crowd, the police retreated.
The demonstrators found themselves confronted by a line of police, blocking the road.
definitions.definition_vi: đối mặt với ai đó để họ không thể tránh nhìn và nghe thấy bạn, đặc biệt là trong tình huống không thân thiện hoặc nguy hiểm

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to make somebody face or deal with an unpleasant or difficult person or situation
examples: He confronted her with a choice between her career or their relationship.
These texts constantly confront the reader with their demanding claims.
definitions.definition_vi: làm cho ai đó phải đối mặt hoặc giải quyết một người hoặc một tình huống khó chịu hoặc khó chịu

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to have something in front of you that you have to deal with or react to
examples: Most people when confronted with a horse will pat it.
definitions.definition_vi: có cái gì đó trước mặt bạn mà bạn phải giải quyết hoặc phản ứng lại

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: unable to think clearly or to understand what is happening or what somebody is saying
examples: I'm confused—say all that again.
I'm getting really confused now. What has that got to do with it?
He was depressed and in a confused state of mind.
a confused look/expression
teenagers who are confused about their sexuality
People are confused about all the different labels on food these days.
She seemed confused by the question.
definitions.definition_vi: không thể suy nghĩ rõ ràng hoặc hiểu những gì đang xảy ra hoặc những gì ai đó đang nói

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: not clear or easy to understand
examples: The children gave a confused account of what had happened.
His mind was crowded with confused thoughts.
A confused situation followed the military coup.
definitions.definition_vi: không rõ ràng hoặc dễ hiểu

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: difficult to understand; not clear
examples: The instructions on the box are very confusing.
a confusing situation/experience
confusing messages/signals
a confusing array of options
This is where it all starts to get really confusing.
Beginners may find the terminology confusing.
The new signs will be very confusing for tourists.
All this information can be confusing to the user.
The site is somewhat confusing to navigate.
It would be confusing to have two set of regulations for a single country.
definitions.definition_vi: khó hiểu; không rõ ràng

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: permission to do something, especially given by somebody in authority
examples: SEE ALSO age of consent
The written consent of a parent is required.
Children under 16 cannot give consent to medical treatment.
to refuse/withhold your consent
He is charged with taking a car without the owner's consent.
definitions.definition_vi: sự cho phép làm điều gì đó, đặc biệt là do người có thẩm quyền đưa ra

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: agreement about something
examples: She was chosen as leader by common consent (= everyone agreed to the choice).
By mutual consent they didn't go out (= they both agreed not to).
definitions.definition_vi: thỏa thuận về điều gì đó

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: an official document giving permission for something
examples: Your family, in effect, signs the consent for you.
definitions.definition_vi: một tài liệu chính thức cho phép một cái gì đó

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: as a result; therefore
examples: LANGUAGE BANK AT because of
This poses a threat to agriculture and the food chain, and consequently to human health.
She failed her exams and was consequently unable to start her studies at college.
definitions.definition_vi: kết quả là; Vì vậy

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to protect something and prevent it from being changed or destroyed
examples: SEE ALSO conservation
new laws to conserve wildlife in the area
definitions.definition_vi: để bảo vệ một cái gì đó và ngăn chặn nó bị thay đổi hoặc phá hủy

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to use as little of something as possible so that it lasts a long time
examples: Help to conserve energy by insulating your home.
Renewable energy resources can help conserve fossil fuels and reduce carbon emissions.
definitions.definition_vi: sử dụng càng ít thứ gì càng tốt để nó tồn tại được lâu

definitions.definition: to be formed from the people or things mentioned
definitions.definition_vi: bao gồm, gồm có những người hoặc vật được nhắc đến
examples: The committee consists of ten members.
Their diet consists largely of vegetables.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to make a position of power or success stronger so that it is more likely to continue
examples: With this new movie he has consolidated his position as the country's leading director.
Italy consolidated their lead with a second goal.
definitions.definition_vi: làm cho vị trí quyền lực hoặc thành công trở nên mạnh mẽ hơn để có nhiều khả năng tiếp tục

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to join things together into one; to be joined into one
examples: All the debts have been consolidated.
consolidated accounts
The two companies consolidated for greater efficiency.
definitions.definition_vi: kết hợp mọi thứ lại thành một; được tham gia thành một

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: happening all the time or repeatedly
examples: There were constant interruptions.
a constant stream of visitors all day
The ruined buildings serve as a constant reminder of the war.
The constant threat of violence from the other inmates was hard to deal with.
Doctors are under constant pressure to treat more and more patients.
Babies need constant attention.
This entrance is in constant use.
definitions.definition_vi: xảy ra mọi lúc hoặc nhiều lần

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: that does not change
examples: The car was travelling at a constant speed of 50 mph.
The samples need to be stored at a constant temperature.
Crime levels remain constant.
Ross was his most constant and loyal friend.
definitions.definition_vi: điều đó không thay đổi

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: connected with the constitution of a country or an organization
examples: constitutional government/reform
a constitutional amendment
She had long advocated constitutional reform.
definitions.definition_vi: liên quan đến hiến pháp của một quốc gia hoặc một tổ chức

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: allowed or limited by the constitution of a country or an organization
examples: OPPOSITE unconstitutional
They can't pass this law. It's not constitutional.
constitutional rights
a constitutional monarchy (= a country with a king or queen whose power is controlled by a set of laws and basic principles)
definitions.definition_vi: được cho phép hoặc bị giới hạn bởi hiến pháp của một quốc gia hoặc một tổ chức

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: related to the body’s ability to stay healthy, be strong and fight illness
examples: constitutional remedies
definitions.definition_vi: liên quan đến khả năng của cơ thể để giữ được sức khỏe, cường tráng và chống lại bệnh tật

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a thing that limits something, or limits your freedom to do something
examples: SYNONYM restriction
constraints of time/money/space
financial/economic/legal/political constraints
This decision will impose serious constraints on all schools.
definitions.definition_vi: một điều mà hạn chế một cái gì đó, hoặc hạn chế quyền tự do của bạn để làm điều gì đó

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: strict control over the way that you behave or are allowed to behave
examples: At last we could relax and talk without constraint.
definitions.definition_vi: kiểm soát chặt chẽ cách bạn cư xử hoặc được phép cư xử

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a person who knows a lot about a particular subject and is employed to give advice about it to other people
examples: SEE ALSO management consultant
a technology/design consultant
She is clearly being coached by image consultants.
the president’s consultant on economic affairs
He was happy to act as a consultant to the company.
definitions.definition_vi: người biết nhiều về một chủ đề cụ thể và được tuyển dụng để đưa ra lời khuyên về chủ đề đó cho người khác

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a hospital doctor of the highest rank who is a specialist in a particular area of medicine
examples: COMPARE registrar
a consultant in obstetrics
a consultant surgeon
definitions.definition_vi: một bác sĩ bệnh viện có cấp bậc cao nhất là chuyên gia trong một lĩnh vực y học cụ thể

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to use something, especially fuel, energy or time
examples: The electricity industry consumes large amounts of fossil fuels.
25 per cent of the world’s population consumes 80 per cent of the planet’s resources.
definitions.definition_vi: sử dụng cái gì đó, đặc biệt là nhiên liệu, năng lượng hoặc thời gian

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to eat or drink something
examples: Before he died, he had consumed a large quantity of alcohol.
a half-consumed loaf of bread
Red meat should be consumed in moderation.
definitions.definition_vi: ăn hoặc uống cái gì đó

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to fill somebody with a strong feeling
examples: Carolyn was consumed with guilt.
Rage consumed him.
definitions.definition_vi: làm ai đó tràn ngập cảm giác mạnh mẽ

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to completely destroy something
examples: The hotel was quickly consumed by fire.
definitions.definition_vi: phá hủy hoàn toàn cái gì đó

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the act of communicating with somebody, especially regularly
examples: I don't have much contact with my uncle.
We've been unable to establish radio contact with the pilot.
She's lost contact with (= no longer sees or writes to) her son.
I finally made contact with (= succeeded in speaking to or meeting) her in Paris.
There is little contact between the two organizations.
We're no longer in regular contact.
The Foreign Office is currently in close contact with the Indian authorities.
Have you kept in contact with any of your friends from college (= do you still see them or speak or write to them)?
The organization put me in contact with other people in a similar position (= gave me their addresses or phone numbers).
Anyone with any information about the incident is asked to get in contact with the police (= phone them or go to see them).
two people avoiding eye contact (= avoiding looking directly at each other)
Please ensure we have your contact number (= phone number) in case we need to reschedule.
I'll give you my contact details (= phone number, email address, etc.)
The society's website provides contact information.
definitions.definition_vi: hành động giao tiếp với ai đó, đặc biệt là thường xuyên

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the state of meeting somebody or having to deal with something
examples: She always avoided contact with the press.
He'd prefer a job where he doesn't have to be in direct contact with the public.
In her job she often comes into contact with (= meets) lawyers.
Children should be brought into contact with poetry at an early age.
definitions.definition_vi: trạng thái gặp ai đó hoặc phải đối phó với điều gì đó

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: an occasion on which you meet or communicate with somebody; a relationship with somebody
examples: Even the US, which has no embassy there, is beginning to forge contacts.
We have good contacts with the local community.
The company has maintained trade contacts with India.
definitions.definition_vi: một dịp mà bạn gặp hoặc giao tiếp với ai đó; một mối quan hệ với ai đó

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a person that you know, especially somebody who can be helpful to you in your work
examples: social/personal contacts
I've made some useful contacts in journalism.
She has several contacts in New York.
He has a contact at the White House.
definitions.definition_vi: một người mà bạn biết, đặc biệt là một người nào đó có thể giúp ích cho bạn trong công việc

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: the state of touching something
examples: a fear of physical contact
The disease is spread by contact.
infections transmitted through sexual contact
His fingers were briefly in contact with the ball.
This substance should not come into contact with food.
This pesticide kills insects on contact (= as soon as it touches them).
This chemical is liable to explode on contact with water.
She blushed at the sudden contact of his hand against her arm.
definitions.definition_vi: trạng thái chạm vào một cái gì đó

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: an electrical connection
examples: The switches close the contacts and complete the circuit.
definitions.definition_vi: một kết nối điện

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: a contact lens (= a small round piece of thin plastic that you put on your eye to help you see better)
definitions.definition_vi: một kính áp tròng (= một miếng nhựa mỏng tròn nhỏ mà bạn đeo vào mắt để giúp bạn nhìn rõ hơn)

definitions.label: Meaning 8

definitions.definition_vi: một người gần đây đã ở gần một người mắc bệnh truyền nhiễm và do đó có thể đã bị lây nhiễm từ họ

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the act of communicating with somebody, especially regularly
examples: I don't have much contact with my uncle.
We've been unable to establish radio contact with the pilot.
She's lost contact with (= no longer sees or writes to) her son.
I finally made contact with (= succeeded in speaking to or meeting) her in Paris.
There is little contact between the two organizations.
We're no longer in regular contact.
The Foreign Office is currently in close contact with the Indian authorities.
Have you kept in contact with any of your friends from college (= do you still see them or speak or write to them)?
The organization put me in contact with other people in a similar position (= gave me their addresses or phone numbers).
Anyone with any information about the incident is asked to get in contact with the police (= phone them or go to see them).
two people avoiding eye contact (= avoiding looking directly at each other)
Please ensure we have your contact number (= phone number) in case we need to reschedule.
I'll give you my contact details (= phone number, email address, etc.)
The society's website provides contact information.
definitions.definition_vi: hành động giao tiếp với ai đó, đặc biệt là thường xuyên

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the state of meeting somebody or having to deal with something
examples: She always avoided contact with the press.
He'd prefer a job where he doesn't have to be in direct contact with the public.
In her job she often comes into contact with (= meets) lawyers.
Children should be brought into contact with poetry at an early age.
definitions.definition_vi: trạng thái gặp ai đó hoặc phải đối phó với điều gì đó

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: an occasion on which you meet or communicate with somebody; a relationship with somebody
examples: Even the US, which has no embassy there, is beginning to forge contacts.
We have good contacts with the local community.
The company has maintained trade contacts with India.
definitions.definition_vi: một dịp mà bạn gặp hoặc giao tiếp với ai đó; một mối quan hệ với ai đó

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a person that you know, especially somebody who can be helpful to you in your work
examples: social/personal contacts
I've made some useful contacts in journalism.
She has several contacts in New York.
He has a contact at the White House.
definitions.definition_vi: một người mà bạn biết, đặc biệt là một người nào đó có thể giúp ích cho bạn trong công việc

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: the state of touching something
examples: a fear of physical contact
The disease is spread by contact.
infections transmitted through sexual contact
His fingers were briefly in contact with the ball.
This substance should not come into contact with food.
This pesticide kills insects on contact (= as soon as it touches them).
This chemical is liable to explode on contact with water.
She blushed at the sudden contact of his hand against her arm.
definitions.definition_vi: trạng thái chạm vào một cái gì đó

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: an electrical connection
examples: The switches close the contacts and complete the circuit.
definitions.definition_vi: một kết nối điện

definitions.label: Meaning 7

definitions.definition_vi: một kính áp tròng (= một miếng nhựa mỏng tròn nhỏ mà bạn đeo vào mắt để giúp bạn nhìn rõ hơn)

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: if something contains something else, it has that thing inside it or as part of it
examples: This drink doesn't contain any alcohol.
The documents contain sensitive information.
Electronic products contain hazardous materials that cannot be deposited in landfills.
His account contained an element of truth.
to contain an amount/a number/a level of something
He handed over a brown envelope containing a hundred dollar bills.
The fish were found to contain traces of mercury.
The bottle contains (= can hold) two litres.
He said he was opposed to some of the provisions contrained in the bill.
The stories contained within these pages are highly enjoyable.
definitions.definition_vi: nếu thứ gì đó chứa thứ khác thì nó có thứ đó bên trong hoặc là một phần của nó

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to keep your feelings under control
examples: SYNONYM restrain
She was unable to contain her excitement.
She could hardly contain her excitement.
I was so furious I just couldn't contain myself (= I had to express my feelings).
definitions.definition_vi: để giữ cảm xúc của bạn trong tầm kiểm soát

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to prevent something harmful from spreading or getting worse
examples: to contain an epidemic
Government forces have failed to contain the rebellion.
definitions.definition_vi: để ngăn chặn một cái gì đó có hại lây lan hoặc trở nên tồi tệ hơn

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a box, bottle, etc. in which something can be stored or transported
examples: a plastic container
Food will last longer if kept in an airtight container.
These women carry heavy containers of water over long distances.
containers for nuclear materials
definitions.definition_vi: cái hộp, cái chai, v.v... trong đó cái gì đó có thể được cất giữ hoặc vận chuyển

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a large metal or wooden box of a standard size in which goods are packed so that they can easily be lifted onto a ship, train, etc. to be transported
examples: a shipping container
a container ship (= one designed to transport such containers)
definitions.definition_vi: một hộp lớn bằng kim loại hoặc gỗ có kích thước tiêu chuẩn, trong đó hàng hóa được đóng gói sao cho có thể dễ dàng nâng lên tàu, tàu hỏa, v.v. để vận chuyển

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a box or pot made of wood, clay, plastic, etc. for growing plants in
examples: COMPARE flowerpot
Planting bulbs in containers is a great alternative if you don't have a garden.
definitions.definition_vi: hộp hoặc chậu làm bằng gỗ, đất sét, nhựa, v.v. để trồng cây ở

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a competition in which people try to win something
examples: SEE ALSO beauty contest
to hold a singing/talent contest
to enter/win a contest
She was awarded the first prize in an essay contest .
It was a close contest between two evenly matched crews.
He said he had enjoyed the contest with his rival for the title .
a contest to win a free tickets to the concert
definitions.definition_vi: một cuộc cạnh tranh trong đó mọi người cố gắng giành chiến thắng một cái gì đó

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a struggle to gain control or power
examples: the leadership/presidential contest
Both parties are predicting victory in this close contest.
a contest for the leadership of the party
a contest between traditional and liberal views
It looks like being a close-fought contest with the Conservatives.
the contest to gain control of the party
definitions.definition_vi: một cuộc đấu tranh để giành quyền kiểm soát hoặc quyền lực

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: used to say that one side in a competition is so much stronger or better than the other that it is sure to win easilyWord Origin
examples: late 16th cent. (as a verb in the sense ‘swear to, attest’): from Latin contestari ‘call upon to witness, initiate (by calling witnesses)’, from con- ‘together’ + testare ‘to witness’. The senses ‘wrangle, struggle for’ arose in the early 17th cent., which gave rise to the current noun and verb senses.
definitions.definition_vi: dùng để nói rằng trong một cuộc thi đấu, một bên mạnh hơn hoặc giỏi hơn bên kia rất nhiều nên chắc chắn sẽ thắng dễ dàngNguồn gốc từ

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: happening or existing for a period of time without being interrupted
examples: Recovery after the accident will be a continuous process that may take several months.
The organization aims to create a culture of continuous improvement .
a continuous stream of data
a continuous flow of knowledge, information and understanding
The rain has been almost continuous for weeks.
She was in continuous employment until the age of sixty-five.
definitions.definition_vi: xảy ra hoặc tồn tại trong một khoảng thời gian mà không bị gián đoạn

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: spreading in a line or over an area without any spaces
examples: a continuous flow of traffic
a continuous stream of lava from the volcano
the largest continuous tropical forest in Central America
definitions.definition_vi: trải dài theo đường hoặc trên một khu vực không có khoảng trống

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: repeated many times
examples: SYNONYM continual
For four days the town suffered continuous attacks.
definitions.definition_vi: lặp đi lặp lại nhiều lần

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: connected with the form of a verb (for example I am waiting or It is raining) that is made from a part of be and the present participle. Progressive forms are used to express an action that continues for a period of time.
examples: the continuous tenses
definitions.definition_vi: được kết nối với dạng động từ (ví dụ: Tôi đang đợi hoặc Trời đang mưa) được tạo thành từ một phần của be và phân từ hiện tại. Các hình thức tiến bộ được sử dụng để diễn tả một hành động tiếp tục trong một khoảng thời gian.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a person or company that has a contract to do work or provide goods or services for another company
examples: SEE ALSO subcontractor
a building/roofing/electrical contractor
a defence/security/military/civilian contractor
a private/an independent contractor
to employ an outside contractor
definitions.definition_vi: một người hoặc công ty có hợp đồng làm việc hoặc cung cấp hàng hóa hoặc dịch vụ cho một công ty khác

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a difference between two or more people or things that you can see clearly when they are compared or put close together; the fact of comparing two or more things in order to show the differences between them
examples: The two cities make an interesting contrast.
There is an obvious contrast between the cultures of East and West.
In contrast, the south suffered very little hurricane damage.
The situation when we arrived was in marked contrast to the news reports.
The poverty of her childhood stands in total contrast to her life in Hollywood.
The company lost $7 million this quarter in contrast to a profit of $6.2 million a year earlier.
to show a sharp/stark/striking contrast with something
A wool jacket complements the silk trousers and provides an interesting contrast in texture.
When you look at their new system, ours seems very old-fashioned by contrast.
Careful contrast of the two plans shows some important differences.
definitions.definition_vi: sự khác biệt giữa hai hoặc nhiều người hoặc nhiều thứ mà bạn có thể thấy rõ khi chúng được so sánh hoặc đặt gần nhau; thực tế so sánh hai hoặc nhiều thứ để chỉ ra sự khác biệt giữa chúng

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a person or thing that is clearly different from somebody/something else
examples: The work you did today is quite a contrast to (= very much better/worse than) what you did last week.
definitions.definition_vi: một người hoặc vật rõ ràng là khác biệt với ai/cái gì khác

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: differences in colour or in light and dark, used in photographs and paintings to create a special effect
examples: The artist's use of contrast is masterly.
definitions.definition_vi: sự khác biệt về màu sắc hoặc ánh sáng và bóng tối, được sử dụng trong ảnh và tranh vẽ để tạo hiệu ứng đặc biệt

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: the amount of difference between light and dark in a photograph or the picture on a television screen
examples: Use this button to adjust the contrast.
definitions.definition_vi: mức độ khác biệt giữa ánh sáng và bóng tối trong một bức ảnh hoặc hình ảnh trên màn hình tivi

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a gift or payment that is made to a person or an organization in order to help pay for something
examples: SYNONYM donation
All contributions will be gratefully received.
We rely entirely on voluntary contributions.
campaign contributions
to make a substantial contribution to charity
valuable contributions towards the upkeep of the cathedral
She argued that a greater contribution towards reducing Britain's record debts should be asked of the better off.
Financial contributions from individuals paid for office and printing expenses.
definitions.definition_vi: một món quà hoặc khoản thanh toán được thực hiện cho một người hoặc một tổ chức để giúp thanh toán cho một cái gì đó

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a sum of money that you pay regularly to your employer or the government in order to pay for benefits such as health insurance, a pension, etc.
examples: SEE ALSO defined contribution
pension contributions
National Insurance contributions
You can increase your monthly contributions to the pension plan.
Pension funds base retirement income on the level of contributions from employees and employers.
definitions.definition_vi: một số tiền mà bạn phải trả thường xuyên cho người sử dụng lao động của bạn hoặc chính phủ để chi trả cho các phúc lợi như bảo hiểm y tế, lương hưu, v.v.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: an action or a service that helps to cause or increase something, usually (but not necessarily) something good or valuable
examples: He made a very positive contribution to the success of the project.
a significant contribution to scientific knowledge
The star is being given the award for his ‘outstanding contribution to the entertainment field’.
This book represents a major contribution to our understanding of the Holocaust.
She feels the world has overlooked his crucial contribution to the development of rock and roll.
the car’s contribution to the greenhouse effect
She was honoured posthumously for her contribution towards the war effort.
These measures would make a valuable contribution towards reducing industrial accidents.
She says the US needs to do more to recognize the contributions of women and minorities to society.
They studied the relative contribution of various risk factors for suicide.
definitions.definition_vi: một hành động hoặc một dịch vụ giúp gây ra hoặc tăng cường một cái gì đó, thường (nhưng không nhất thiết) một cái gì đó tốt hoặc có giá trị

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: an item that forms part of a book, magazine, website broadcast, discussion, etc.
examples: All contributions for the May issue must be received by Friday.
an important contribution to the debate
Thank you for your contributions to the blog.
There are no contributions by scholars based in North America.
definitions.definition_vi: một mục là một phần của một cuốn sách, tạp chí, chương trình phát sóng trên trang web, cuộc thảo luận, v.v.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: the act of giving something, especially money, to help a person or an organization
examples: The institute is totally funded by voluntary contribution.
definitions.definition_vi: hành động đưa ra một cái gì đó, đặc biệt là tiền, để giúp đỡ một người hoặc một tổ chức

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the power to make decisions about how a country, an area, an organization, etc. is run
examples: The party expects to gain control of the council in the next election.
Militants have taken control of the town.
The Democrats have lost control of Congress.
A military junta seized control of the country.
The founders eventually regained control of the company.
He defended the tradition of civilian control over the military.
The city is in the control of enemy forces.
The area remains under international control.
definitions.definition_vi: quyền đưa ra quyết định về cách thức điều hành một quốc gia, một khu vực, một tổ chức, v.v.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the ability to make somebody/something do what you want
examples: SEE ALSO self-control
The teacher had no control over the children.
He fought hard to retain control over his work.
She struggled to keep control of her voice.
She lost control of her car on the ice.
He got so angry he lost control (= shouted and said or did things he would not normally do).
Owing to circumstances beyond our control, the flight to Rome has been cancelled.
The situation is under control.
The coach made the team work hard on ball control (= in a ball game).
definitions.definition_vi: khả năng khiến ai/cái gì làm điều bạn muốn

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the act of limiting or managing something; a method of doing this
examples: SEE ALSO birth control
traffic control
talks on arms control
tight controls on government spending
Price controls on food were ended.
exciting advances in the control of malaria
state control of the economy
It was an exercise in damage control (= trying to prevent further damage).
A pest control officer was called in to deal with the rat problem.
definitions.definition_vi: hành động hạn chế hoặc quản lý một cái gì đó; một phương pháp để làm điều này

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: the switches and buttons, etc. that you use to operate a machine or a vehicle
examples: SEE ALSO cruise control
the controls of an aircraft
the control panel
the volume control of a TV
The co-pilot was at the controls when the plane landed.
definitions.definition_vi: các công tắc và nút bấm, v.v. mà bạn sử dụng để vận hành máy móc hoặc phương tiện

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a person, thing or group used as a standard of comparison for checking the results of a scientific experiment; an experiment whose result is known, used for checking working methods
examples: The study showed that women with the disease have had fewer children than the controls.
One group was treated with the new drug, and the control group was given a sugar pill.
definitions.definition_vi: người, vật, nhóm dùng làm tiêu chuẩn so sánh để kiểm tra kết quả thí nghiệm khoa học; một thí nghiệm đã biết kết quả, dùng để kiểm tra phương pháp làm việc

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: a place where orders are given or where checks are made; the people who work in this place
examples: SEE ALSO air traffic control
We went through passport control and into the departure lounge.
definitions.definition_vi: nơi đưa ra mệnh lệnh hoặc nơi thực hiện kiểm tra; những người làm việc ở nơi này

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: (on a computer keyboard) a key that you press when you want to perform a particular operation
definitions.definition_vi: (trên bàn phím máy tính) phím mà bạn nhấn khi muốn thực hiện một thao tác cụ thể

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to direct or manage an organization, an area or a situation
examples: He's reached retiring age, but he's still firmly in control.
There has been some violence after the match, but the police are now in control of the situation.
The elected government is back in control.
definitions.definition_vi: chỉ đạo hoặc quản lý một tổ chức, một khu vực hoặc một tình huống

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to be able to organize your life well and keep calm
examples: In spite of all her family problems, she's really in control.
definitions.definition_vi: để có thể tổ chức cuộc sống của bạn tốt và giữ bình tĩnh

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: to be or become impossible to manage or to control
examples: The children are completely out of control since their father left.
A truck ran out of control on the hill.
definitions.definition_vi: trở nên không thể quản lý hoặc kiểm soát

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: to be being dealt with successfully
examples: Don't worry—everything's under control!
definitions.definition_vi: được giải quyết thành công

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: to succeed in dealing with something so that it does not cause any damage or hurt anyone
examples: It took two hours to bring the fire under control.
Please keep your dog under control!
definitions.definition_vi: thành công trong việc giải quyết việc gì đó để nó không gây ra thiệt hại hoặc làm tổn thương ai

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: tending to follow what is done or considered acceptable by society in general; normal and ordinary, and perhaps not very interesting
examples: OPPOSITE unconventional
conventional behaviour/morality
She's very conventional in her views.
definitions.definition_vi: có xu hướng làm theo những gì được thực hiện hoặc được xã hội nói chung chấp nhận; bình thường và bình thường, và có lẽ không thú vị lắm

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: following what is traditional or the way something has been done for a long time
examples: OPPOSITE unconventional
conventional methods/approaches
It's not a hotel, in the conventional sense, but rather a whole village turned into a hotel.
You can use a microwave or cook it in a conventional oven.
definitions.definition_vi: làm theo những gì truyền thống hoặc cách thức nào đó đã được thực hiện trong một thời gian dài

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: using the usual scientific methods of Western medicine such as artificial drugs and operations
examples: COMPARE alternative medicine
conventional medicine
Conventional treatments for this condition have been only partially successful.
definitions.definition_vi: sử dụng các phương pháp khoa học thông thường của Tây y như thuốc nhân tạo và phẫu thuật

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: not nuclear
examples: conventional forces/weapons
A conventional war would still cause unacceptable devastation.
a conventional power station (= using oil or coal as fuel, rather than nuclear power)
definitions.definition_vi: không hạt nhân

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: the view or belief that most people hold
examples: Conventional wisdom has it that riots only ever happen in cities.
definitions.definition_vi: quan điểm hoặc niềm tin mà hầu hết mọi người nắm giữ

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: an informal talk involving a small group of people or only two; the activity of talking in this way
examples: a phone conversation
The main topic of conversation was the likely outcome of the election.
I tried to make conversation (= to speak in order to appear polite).
I had a long conversation with her the other day.
She was engaged in conversation with a colleague.
to get into conversation with somebody
to get into a conversation with somebody
I overheard a conversation between two colleagues.
We had to listen to endless conversations about high prices and food shortages.
Don was deep in conversation with the girl on his right.
I spent an hour in conversation with him.
The conversation turned to gardening.
Desperately he struggled to keep the conversation going.
I see no point in continuing this conversation.
She tried to steer the conversation away from the topic of marriage.
He felt a sudden alarm at the turn the conversation was taking.
definitions.definition_vi: một cuộc nói chuyện thân mật có sự tham gia của một nhóm nhỏ hoặc chỉ hai người; hoạt động nói chuyện theo cách này

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to change or make something change from one form, purpose, system, etc. to another
examples: They took just nine months to convert the building.
You need to ensure that you've converted the data properly.
The pub is a converted warehouse.
The hotel is going to be converted into a nursing home.
What rate will I get if I convert my dollars into euros?
The system is eco-friendly because the waste heat is converted to electricity.
Japan was at the time still converting from an agricultural economy.
A lot of conventional farmers have converted to organic production.
We've converted from oil to gas central heating.
definitions.definition_vi: thay đổi hoặc thực hiện một cái gì đó thay đổi từ một hình thức, mục đích, hệ thống, vv sang hình thức khác

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to be able to be changed from one form, purpose, or system to another
examples: a sofa that converts into a bed
